terminology-research: Look up requirement and design terms on the web before writing specs. Use to prevent terminology drift in P0–P4.
automation-run: Run automation for an agreed plan using skills in order. Use when the user asks to automate a plan; stop if approval or scope changes.
maintain-adhoc: Update kit skills, rules, or catalogs for process changes. Use when the agent kit itself needs an incremental fix.
implement-reference: Gather plan scope, acceptance criteria, and design constraints before coding. Use at the start of a Do cycle.
memory-reason: Propose what to promote, flush, or archive from recalled memory. Use after reading nav/index each turn.
secretary-route: Map user intent to Cursor roles after the turn brief. Use when choosing builder, reviewer, or other roles; run adaptive-lifecycle when lifecycle_plan is empty.
review-record: Persist review results to docs/reviews or the plan PDCA log. Use after completing a review.
lib-tdd-cycle: Red-Green-Refactor TDD cycle for implementation work. Use when writing application code, fixing failing tests, or when the user asks for TDD or test-first changes.
pm-turn-end: End every agent turn—score the turn, flush chat into episode/nav memory, update next_actions. Use before the final user reply after work finishes. Also after failed tools or when context pressure is high.
automation-record: Write automation run metadata and audit notes after an automation finishes. Use when logging Cursor Automation or agreed-plan automation results.
automation-reference: Check whether an agreed plan is ready for automation. Use before starting Cursor Automation or scheduled agent runs.
implement-record: Write the PDCA Do log on the plan after implementation. Use after coding—not for editing application source.
maintain-bootstrap: Bootstrap a repo after copying the agent kit—AGENTS.md, docs skeleton, memory, hooks. Use on brand-new projects or first kit install.
memory-reference: Read nav.yaml and the memory index before acting. Use at turn start or whenever next_actions may be stale.
memory-record: Update nav.yaml, write an episode, and touch the memory index. Use at turn end after flush; also when repairing missing memory files.
secretary-brief: Write a short turn brief (and nav brief on Loop2) with role rows and gate. Use after memory recall, before executing roles.
role-skill-catalog: Look up which skills and rules belong to each role and phase. Use when unsure what to run next or when maintaining the kit catalog.
patch-reference: Decide whether a change is a small patch or needs full builder scope. Use before hotfixes.
patch-record: Record a patch on the plan PDCA log. Use after a hotfix—not for writing application code.
context-guard: Detect context pressure, nav mismatch, and summarize risk at the start of a turn. Use first on every message, especially long chats or after Cursor summarize.
design-reference: Search existing design, requirements, ADR, and glossary before writing. Use when checking prior decisions or preparing a design edit.
landscape-research: Broad-then-narrow web research for architecture and policy questions. Use for exploratory research; not for single term definitions.
plan-evaluate: Evaluate one plan file for drift and at-risk status. Use mid-flight when a plan may be stale.
evaluate-record: Persist mid-project evaluation results to docs/evaluations or plan Evaluate rows. Use after plan-evaluate or project-evaluate.
plan-record: Create implementation plans under .agents/plans after design gates and user confirmation. Use when slicing work into Do units—not for writing specs.
review-reference: Gather git diff, plan criteria, and design for a review. Use at the start of Check.
memory-refine: Archive stale threads and supersede outdated memory entries. Use after full evaluate and critique when the index is noisy.
plan-reference: Search plans and verify Do readiness against acceptance criteria. Use before coding or when checking plan status.
project-evaluate: Evaluate the whole project across design, plans, reviews, and repo health. Use at milestones.
patch-conduct: Apply a small fix within file/line caps. Use for hotfixes after patch scope was approved.
maintain-scripts: Inventory and review scripts under skills/*/scripts/. Use when auditing or refactoring kit helper scripts.
evaluate-reference: Gather plans, docs, and git for a mid-flight evaluation. Use at milestones—not every turn.
cursor-capabilities-reference: List available Cursor tools (browser, Shell, MCP, open_resource) before claiming something is unavailable. Use when verifying URLs, screenshots, or terminals.
implement-conduct: Implement the agreed plan with TDD and minimal diffs. Use when coding features or fixes inside plan scope.
lib-review-vmodel: V-model review checklist mapping requirements, design, plan criteria, and tests. Use when reviewing code, writing review notes, or checking acceptance criteria against design and requirements.
lifecycle-reference: Read project phase, gates, and lifecycle docs when aligning navigation. Use on Loop2, re-anchor, or before recording plans/design—not every lightweight turn.
action-evaluate: Score whether this turn advanced the goal and followed the plan. Use after finishing work or answering, before saving memory.
maintain-reference: Inventory kit layout, catalogs, and AGENTS stack docs before changing the kit. Use before bootstrap or ad hoc maintenance.
memory-critique: Self-RAG style check that recalled memory supports this turn. Use after a full turn score—not on greetings or mini scores.
brownfield-reference: Inventory an existing repo and fill reverse-engineering templates before new requirements. Use on legacy codebases or when adaptive-lifecycle says brownfield first.
maintain-record: Write kit artifacts (rules, skills, AGENTS.md, docs) after maintenance work. Use after bootstrap or ad hoc kit edits.
secretary-record: Persist the brief into episodes via memory-record. Use at turn end after flush.
memory-flush: Flush chat content into external memory levels before writing files. Use at turn end, especially when context is nearly full.
lib-memory-io: Contracts for writing nav.yaml, episodes, index, and audit-log. Use at turn end, after flush, or when repairing missing memory directories.
design-record: Write design and requirements markdown under docs/ with Facts/Assumptions/Open. Use when drafting charters, 要求, 要件, or design docs—not plans or ADR.
doc-record: Write ADR and glossary entries under docs/. Use when capturing architecture decisions or term definitions—not design folders or plans.
secretary-reference: Gather light context for briefing after memory recall. Use when preparing the turn brief.
pm-turn-start: Start every agent turn—read nav memory, detect context pressure, draft a short turn plan and pick roles. Use at the beginning of user messages, before coding or editing. Also when resuming after summarize or when unsure what to do next.
adaptive-lifecycle-plan: Recommend which project phases to run, what to skip, and Cursor mode from a new or changed goal. Use at project start or when scope jumps; wait for user Go before advancing.
review-conduct: Review code against plan criteria, requirements, and design (V-model). Use at Check time after gathering review context.
cursor-tool-select: Pick the right Cursor tool for the job (WebSearch, browser, Shell). Use when researching terms, checking UI, or running commands.
lib-doc-frontmatter: Shared YAML frontmatter and Facts/Assumptions/Open section rules for design, plan, and ADR markdown. Use when writing or reviewing docs under docs/design, docs/requirements, docs/adr, or .agents/plans.
design-deliberate: Facilitate design options and tradeoffs before writing specs. Use when requirements are unclear or the user wants choices A/B/C.
role-execute: Run the role skill list from the turn brief in order inside this chat. Use after routing—never via Subagent.
